author: woj_zaremba
text:
(3 / 4)
and furthermore, many important advances in the history of AI, both within OpenAI and outside of it, can be seen as a direct consequence of merely trying to obtain better baselines.

author: woj_zaremba
text:
(2 / 4)
The latter is critical, as many methods that “look good on paper” aren’t actually good because of weak baselines and lack of rigor when comparing to baselines;

author: woj_zaremba
text:
(1 / 4)
At OpenAI, our primary goal is really to solve the problem at hand.  Thus, we care deeply about understanding which part of a system contributed to performance, so as not to have false beliefs.  Likewise, we spend a lot of time on building excellent baselines and metrics.

author: woj_zaremba
text:
@dmvaldman Solving technical alignment is insufficient to ensure that AGI will play out well. It's just one big piece of the puzzle.

I believe in iterative deployment as the means to get it right.

author: woj_zaremba
text:
ML systems are often optimized for what is easy to measure rather than what we care about (misalignment). 
E.g., social networks might maximize engagement rather than truthfulness. Such optimization leads to the proliferation of fake news, as they spread 5x faster than real news.

author: woj_zaremba

First, we have to figure out how to align our models. This is not a fully solved problem.

Don't know yet what's the right answer to the second question.
